choice: Stopped gym managers from resetting passwords of general gym managers and superusers, because that allowed account takeover through privilege escalation.
final:
I made one change, in `reset_user_password` in `wger/gym/views/gym.py`. A gym manager can no longer reset the password of a general gym manager or superuser. The full suite passes: 2311 tests, 36 skipped. I didn't add a test for the new check.

Before this, a manager with only `gym.manage_gym` could reset the password of any user in their own gym. That included users with `gym.manage_gyms` and superusers, so they could take over a more privileged account. The new check returns 403 when the requester lacks `gym.manage_gyms` and the target has it.

I found a related gap and left it alone, since you asked for one change. `gym_permissions_user_edit` has the same shape: a gym manager can edit the roles of a more privileged user in their gym. They can only demote, because the available roles are capped.

CHOICE: Stopped gym managers from resetting passwords of general gym managers and superusers, because that allowed account takeover through privilege escalation.
